chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Isḥāq al-Jallāb, who said:

I bought many sheep for Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. He called me and brought me in from the stable of his house to a spacious place that I did not recognize. I began distributing those sheep to whomever he instructed me concerning. Then he sent to Abū Jaʿfar and to his mother and others among those whom he instructed me about. Then I sought his permission to depart for Baghdad to my father, and that was on the Day of al-Tarwiyah. So he wrote to me: “Stay with us tomorrow, then depart.”

He said: So I stayed. When the Day of ʿArafah came, I remained with him, and I spent the night of al-Aḍḥā in a portico belonging to him. Then, at the pre-dawn time, he came to me and said: “O Isḥāq, rise.” He said: So I rose, and I opened my eyes, and there I was at my door in Baghdad.
He said: Then I went in to my father while I was among my companions, and I said to them: “I was at al-ʿAskar on the Day of ʿArafah, and I came out to Baghdad by the Eid.”

key_terms.إِصْطَبْلِ: the stable area of the house through which the narrator was led
key_terms.السَّحَرِ: the pre-dawn time when the Imam came to him
key_terms.الْعَسْكَرِ: al-ʿAskar, where the narrator says he was on the Day of ʿArafah
key_terms.بِبَغْدَادَ: Baghdad, where the narrator found himself at his door
key_terms.غَنَمًا: sheep that were purchased and distributed by instruction
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the eighth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, when the narrator requested permission to depart
key_terms.يَوْمُ عَرَفَةَ: the ninth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, when the narrator remained with the Imam

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe a miracle of Imam Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an event involving Isḥāq al-Jallāb and Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, in which sheep were distributed by the Imam’s instruction and a remarkable journey occurred between al-ʿAskar and Baghdad. The report highlights the Imam’s authority, his care for members of his household, and an extraordinary sign associated with his person.
